cap: Estrogen at puberty everts the columnar endocervical lining onto the ectocervix, and the acidic vagina converts it to squamous epithelium by metaplasia. The band between the original and the active squamocolumnar junction is the transformation zone, whose immature metaplastic cells are the cells high-risk HPV transforms. After menopause the junction retreats into the canal, where a spatula alone misses it.
teach: Read the top panel left to right as a walk up the cervix: mature squamous ectocervix, then the transformation zone, then mucus-secreting columnar endocervix. Read the bottom panel as a lifetime. A Pap sample is only as good as its coverage of the zone, so the brush matters most when the junction has moved into the canal.
